summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for persistent cough and malaise. He had been treated outpatient for presumed pneumonia with amoxicillin, prednisone, and azithromycin without improvement, followed by a brief course of levofloxacin. Admission chest X-ray revealed a right middle lobe infiltrate consistent with pneumonia. He was started on intravenous vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to ceftriaxone and levofloxacin. His hyponatremia (Na 127) was attributed to hypovolemia, improved with fluid resuscitation, and his home diuretics were held. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. His diabetes was managed with insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He remained stable, with resolving symptoms, and was discharged on oral levofloxacin to complete a 7-day course, with instructions to follow up on sodium levels and repeat chest imaging.
